assessment: This paper explores how diverse forms of inhibition impact firing rates in models for cortical circuits. In particular, the paper studies how the network operating point affects the balance of direct inhibition from SOM inhibitory neurons to pyramidal cells, and disinhibition from SOM inhibitory input to PV inhibitory neurons. This is an important issue as these two inhibitory pathways have largely been studied in isolation. A combination of analytical calculations and direct numerical simulations provides convincing evidence that the interplay of these inhibitory circuits can separately control network gain and stability.
